text:
Mia Patel: Heads-up — noticed inconsistent env-var/config precedence across SDKs and the CLI. CLI (go) will read ~/.redwood/token, but node/python SDKs only check REDWOOD_API_KEY. This trips up the sample app and our quickstart. Anyone else seen onboarding friction from this?

Kevin Zhang: Yup. Got a support ticket where user had `~/.redwood` token from the console, ran `npm start` and got 401s. Node SDK didn't fall back. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:

Samir Rao: Repro steps I used:
```
# user exported org but not API key
export REDWOOD_ORG=my-acme
# CLI login writes ~/.redwood/token
redwood login --org my-acme
# sample app (node) fails because it expects REDWOOD_API_KEY
node examples/chat.js
```
It felt surprising. Also noticed REDWOOD_ORG vs REDWOOD_PROJECT semantics differ between SDKs (org vs workspace).

Alex Gomez: Can confirm. Python SDK currently reads both env and ~/.redwood, node only env. That's why the quickstart README instructs `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` which is redundant if you used `redwood login`. We should make parity: env > local token file > OS keychain.

Mia Patel: Agreed on a clear precedence order. Proposal: 1) REDWOOD_API_KEY env override, 2) REDWOOD_SERVICE_TOKEN (project-scoped) env next, 3) ~/.redwood token file (CLI-produced), 4) platform keychain. Also standardize names: REDWOOD_API_KEY (global), REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY (project-scoped) and REDWOOD_ORG remains for default routing. Thoughts?

Kevin Zhang: I like it. Two UX notes: 1) sample apps should detect and log which credential source they used (so users don't guess), 2) when a token rotates and API returns 401, SDK should try fallback sources once and emit a clearer error like `no-valid-credentials` with hint to re-run `redwood login`.

Samir Rao: For rotation specifically, can we add a header on 401 from our auth gateway e.g. `x-redwood-auth-retry: true` when token is expired vs `x-redwood-auth-retry: false` for other auth failures? Then SDKs can surface a friendly message and optionally open browser to re-login from the app.

Alex Gomez: Implementation plan I'm thinking for node SDK: add a small credential-loader that runs at init and a `refreshOn401` flag. Pseudocode: 
```
const creds = loadCreds({ envFirst: true })
client = new Redwood({ apiKey: creds.key, refreshOn401: true })
client.on('auth:expired', () => console.log('token expired — run `redwood login`'))
```
I'll open a PR to add loader + event hook. Tests: simulate 401 with expired token header and assert event emitted.

Mia Patel: Nice. Also let's update sample app README to include a diagnostic command: `redwood whoami` that prints effective org/project and credential source. That will cut down support noise.

Kevin Zhang: Agree. For naming, prefer `REDWOOD_PROJECT` over `REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY` to avoid confusion with project id vs token. Keep `REDWOOD_SERVICE_TOKEN` for long-lived service tokens. Document precedence clearly in the SDK READMEs.

Samir Rao: I'll file a short spec doc and link in the PR: https://go/redwood/specs/cred-precedence (placeholder). Also recommend we add a small telemetry event (opt-in) when SDK falls back to file so we can measure how many users rely on CLI tokens.

devx-bot: Created issue RDW-7894: "Standardize credential precedence across SDKs + CLI; diagnostic whoami; token rotation handling" (assigned to @Alex Gomez).

Alex Gomez: I'll take RDW-7894. Plan: PR for node SDK + sample apps updated this week, follow-up for python after. Will add unit tests and integration test against local auth mock.

Mia Patel: Awesome — thanks. Can we also add a tiny migration note in the console login flow: "Want quickstart with samples? set REDWOOD_API_KEY or run `redwood login` — both work now" once we change precedence so users don't get surprised.

Kevin Zhang: :thumbsup: leaving a slash of acceptance criteria here: 1) doc updated, 2) node SDK loader + tests, 3) sample apps log credential source, 4) CLI whoami command, 5) 401 header change on auth gateway. If all that lands, we should reduce onboarding tickets significantly.

Samir Rao: I'll help verify in staging. Thanks team.
